name: Century Enka Ltd
title: Century Enka Ltd - 500280 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 margin jump (EBITDA margin 11.46%, +948bp YoY) rode on price pass-through and cheap inventory; management now guides operating margin 7-10% vs prior 6-8%, with capex only ~Rs 100 crore and cash piling up.

capex.quote: we are expecting a total CAPEX outlay of over Rs. 100 crores, primarily going into value-added products

triggers.quote: We operated at about 80% for the year in terms of capacity utilization. In the Quarter 4, it was about 85%.

triggers.label: Price hikes passed through since March
triggers.quote: The sharp rise in raw material prices following the Iran conflict enabled us to implement price increases across all product lines.

triggers.label: Op margin range raised to 7-10%
triggers.quote: we now feel that depending on the external scenarios and demand, our operating margin could be in the range of 7% to 10%.

triggers.label: ADD on Chinese NFY imports recommended
triggers.quote: the DGTR has issued a favorable anti-dumping ruling. We now await final notification from the Finance Ministry.

I mean, the discussion is on growth and how to make the company sustainable
We would ideally want to have repeat our Q4 plus volumes, but this is all dependent on so many external factors.

summary.headline: Century Enka Q4 FY26 operating revenue Rs 484 crore (+9% YoY) with EBITDA margin up 948 bps YoY to 11.46%, aided by price pass-through and some low-cost inventory.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sharp YoY profit recovery: volume grew 14% YoY to 20,711 MT and EBITDA rose to Rs 55 crore, with price increases passed through after the Iran-related raw material spike from March. For FY26, revenue fell 15% to Rs 1,705 crore on 6% lower volume, but EBITDA (+29%) and PAT (+52%) improved. Management said the company has raised its indicative operating margin band to 7-10% from 6-8%, though it declined to guide quarterly numbers. Management indicated part of the gain came from consumption of lower-priced raw material, which will fade, and said the Rs 100 crore FY27 capex and renewable power additions will help margins only from H2.

financial_highlights.change: +294 bps YoY; EBITDA Rs 148 crore, +29% YoY

segments.name: Reinforcement (Nylon tire cord, NTCF)
segments.commentary: Q4 sales Rs 245 crore, +21% YoY; FY26 sales Rs 816 crore, -15% YoY. Management says demand from tractor, two-wheeler and truck/bus was robust post GST cut.

segments.name: Filament yarn (incl. polyester industrial yarn)
segments.commentary: Q4 sales Rs 229 crore, +3% YoY; FY26 sales Rs 828 crore, -14% YoY. Finished goods inventory was reduced healthily during the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Indicative operating margin range raised to 7-10% (earlier 6-8%), depending on demand and external conditions; no quarterly guidance given.

Renewable content of power rises from about 36% in FY26 to about 48% after commissioning of additional renewable power, a roughly 12% reduction in power consumption mix; additional capacity expected in FY27.
Expect margin improvement to reflect in Q3 and Q4 FY27 as cost initiatives take effect.
Management would ideally like to repeat Q4-plus volume levels in FY27, but declined to give revenue growth targets.
Polyester tire cord (PTCF) commercial sales expected in H2 FY27 after tire-company approvals.
Anti-dumping duty on nylon filament yarn: DGTR ruling favourable; awaiting Finance Ministry notification. Estimated price impact 10-30% of current FOB value.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex over Rs 100 crore for value-added products, Mother Yarn capacity expansion, power consumption reduction, and fire-risk reconfiguration at old plants at Bharuch.
PTCF (polyester tire cord fabric) capacity about 4 KT per annum; utilisation 75-80% on industrial yarn demand; about Rs 100 crore spent, commissioned about 2.5 years ago.
Capacity addition from the FY27 project about 2-2.5 KT; other projects add value rather than capacity.

Renewable power: company holds 26% equity in a third-party group captive hybrid project; equity contribution under Rs 10 crore; Phase-1 about 15 MW installed, 6-7 MW average output per year; Phase-2 expected to start around Q3 FY27.
Overall capacity utilisation about 80% in FY26 and about 85% in Q4 FY26.
Balance of cash in investments above Rs 400 crore; management says it is being evaluated for growth, including possibly new segments in textiles; no buyback decision.
demand_pricing: Raw material (caprolactam) prices rose sharply from March 2026 after the Iran conflict; company says price increases were passed through across product lines, with some customers' orders booked at earlier rates honoured.
Management says it did not cut production during the conflict and still consumes some older, lower-priced raw material, which will taper and reduce the margin benefit.

Demand drivers were tractor (record FY26 sales after a good monsoon), two-wheelers (above pre-COVID retail levels) and truck/bus; management expects slower growth going forward and tracks monsoon and rural demand.
Radialisation in truck and bus at about 60%, now stabilising; management expects only 1-2% growth in nylon reinforcement demand.
PTCF market in India estimated at about 25 KT, with 80-85% imported.
Chinese imports at low prices persist in commodity yarn; imports are about 20-25% of domestic NFY demand.
Exports are about 4-5% of revenue; management did not clearly say whether rupee depreciation is a net benefit.
Value-added products earn about 20% additional margin over commodity products after conversion costs; commodity nylon filament yarn is about 15-20% of volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA margin is from inventory gains versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split the margin, citing competitive reasons. It said the company actively reduced inventory during the volatile period, and sales volume was a main driver of the Q4 performance.

qa_highlights.question: With over Rs 400 crore in investments and Rs 100 crore capex, will the company consider buyback or higher dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board discussions focus on growth and possible new segments including textiles. It said the buyback request has been conveyed to the Board, which will decide on merits; no decision was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement sustainable once low-cost inventory is used up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged that higher-priced inventory will flow through, but said the operating margin range is now 7-10% versus 6-8% earlier, given cost and power initiatives that phase in from Q3-Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of PTCF approval and when will commercial sales start?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is at Stage 2 of four approval stages with tire companies, with commercial sales expected in H2 FY27. The 4 KT plant has been utilised at 75-80% for industrial yarn.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the nylon filament yarn anti-dumping duty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the duty to lift domestic prices, estimating the impact at 10-30% of current FOB value. It did not quantify the import decline given that the duty is not yet notified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 100 crore FY27 capex capacity-enhancing?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 2-2.5 KT of capacity will be added from the project; most spend is for value-addition, power efficiency and safety, which should improve margins but not add capacity.

risks_watch: Volatile crude and caprolactam prices; the margin benefit from old low-cost inventory will fade in coming quarters.
Chinese commodity imports at low prices; anti-dumping duty still needs Finance Ministry notification.
Slower tractor and two-wheeler demand after a record FY26 driven by a strong monsoon and rural demand; radialisation in truck and bus.
Slow PTCF approval by tire OEMs; commercial sales timing has slipped to H2 FY27 and capacity is only about 4 KT.
Capital allocation: Rs 400+ crore cash and buyback/dividend questions remain open; no Board decision on new projects.
Management gave no margin guidance for specific quarters, and said planning is now quarter-on-quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the pass-through of raw material costs, but guarded on the outlook; management repeatedly declined quantitative guidance on quarterly margins, revenue and buyback, citing external volatility. Answers on margin split, cash deployment and new projects were evasive.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report a strong financial quarter marked by healthy growth across revenue and profits, supported by higher sales volume and effective pass-through of raw material cost increases.
So, we have to evaluate projects which, first of all, have growth potential in India, second, are effectively able to compete against imports from China.
we now feel that depending on the external scenarios and demand, our operating margin could be in the range of 7% to 10%.

adds.what: PTCF (polyester tire cord fabric) capacity addition from FY27 project about 2-2.5 KT/yr
Renewable captive hybrid power: Phase-2 (26% equity stake in third-party group project)

growth.why: Management raised indicative operating margin band to 7-10% (from 6-8%) and gave no revenue growth target; FY27 capex of over Rs 100 crore and ~2-2.5 KT capacity addition are planned, but the margin lift is partly from low-cost inventory that will fade and PTCF sales only start H2 FY27, so backing is partial.
